name: CA-09
label: Safe D

key_factors: Harder's massive financial advantage ($4.7M cash vs. $19K)
Markets price Harder at 96-98% to win
Challenger McBride raised only $52K with no outside support
model.rationale: Harder holds a dominant fundraising edge, a district that leans Democratic by eight points, and prediction markets pricing his win odds at 96-98%. McBride's minimal resources and lack of outside spending give no evidence to move off a Safe D assessment.
model.watch: Any late surge of outside Republican spending or a polling surprise showing a single-digit race would warrant reclassification.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Josh Harder, the Democratic incumbent, seeks another term in a Central Valley district that leans Democratic by about eight points. He has raised over $4 million and holds $4.7 million in cash, while Republican John McBride has raised roughly $52,000 with minimal outside support on either side. No general-election polls are available, and no expert raters have flagged the race as competitive.

Prediction markets on Kalshi and Polymarket price Harder's win probability at 96 to 98 percent. With the incumbent's financial dominance, the district's partisan lean, and no visible challenger momentum, the race sits firmly in Safe D territory, though the absence of polling keeps uncertainty somewhat elevated.
